Introduction

What Is a Digital Signature Certificate?

A Digital Signature Certificate is an electronic equivalent of a physical signature, issued by a licensed Certifying Authority and stored on a secure USB token. It's used to sign documents electronically for government filings — company incorporation, ROC filings, income tax returns, GST filings and more.

A Class 3 DSC is the standard requirement for most company law and tax filings, and is mandatory for directors, authorised signatories and professionals filing on behalf of clients.

Where It's Used

Filings That Require a DSC

🏢

MCA / ROC Filings

Company incorporation, annual returns, and event-based ROC filings all require a DSC from directors or authorised signatories.

🧾

Income Tax Filings

Mandatory for companies and certain categories of taxpayers filing income tax returns and tax audit reports.

🧮

GST Filings

Required for GST registration and return filing for companies and LLPs on the GST portal.

📝

E-Tendering & E-Procurement

Used to sign bids and documents on government e-tendering and procurement portals.

Who Needs One

Individuals & Entities Requiring a DSC

  • Directors of Private Limited, Public Limited and Section 8 Companies
  • Designated partners of LLPs
  • Authorised signatories filing GST or income tax returns on behalf of an entity
  • Professionals, including Chartered Accountants, filing on behalf of clients

Step-by-Step

Application Process & Timeline

1. Document Collection

We gather identity and address proof for the individual the DSC will be issued to.

2. Video Verification

Certifying Authorities require a short video-based identity verification as part of issuance.

3. Certificate Issuance

Once verified, the DSC is issued and loaded onto a secure USB token, typically within 1 to 2 working days.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN card of the applicant
  • Aadhaar or another government-issued address proof
  • Passport-size photograph
  • Active mobile number and email for video verification
